utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Good to see you, Raymond. What's been on your mind this week?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I'm really worried about my father. He's 82 and in a care home. I visited last Tuesday and he looked terrible. He told me the night staff don't feed him properly and they leave him in soiled sheets for hours.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That sounds very distressing to witness. Caregiver burnout is a real problem in care facilities. Did you speak to the management about it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Management brushed me off. And it's worse than that — he showed me a bruise on his arm. He said one of the night aides grabbed him hard when he was confused. That's elder abuse and no one is doing anything about it.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Seeing a parent suffer is one of the most painful things a person can experience. How is this affecting your own stress levels and sleep?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Of course my sleep is affected but my father is being abused right now. I saw the bruise myself. He says someone is abusing him at that facility and I believe him. What am I supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Your advocacy for your father shows how much you love him. It might be worth looking into moving him to a different facility. Have you researched other options in your area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I can't just move him overnight. I need someone to take this seriously right now. He's being abused every day I leave him there.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I can hear how urgent this feels. Let's talk about how you can manage the anxiety while you work through the practical steps to address his care.
